What makes a good spot

  • Visible to students, families, and the community
  • Safe, not blocking walkways or drivers' view
  • Easy to mount on posts, a wall, or a fence
  • Protected from damage and overgrowth
Marked in red · sign is 3 ft × 4 ft
Option 1

Front Circle by the Flagpole

MountingTwo posts in the planter, like the bond measure sign beside it

Why it works

  • The center of the front entrance. Students, parents, and visitors all walk past it.
  • Next to the flagpole, a natural place for a school award.
  • The planter already holds a post-mounted sign, so we know posts work here.
Marked in red · sign is 3 ft × 4 ft
Option 2

Under the Tam High Hawks Marquee

MountingLow posts in the planting bed

Why it works

  • Faces the street, so the whole community sees it, not just students.
  • Puts the award right under the school's name.
  • Everyone driving into the lot passes it.
Marked in red · sign is 3 ft × 4 ft
Option 3

Front Lawn by the Campus Directory

MountingPosts set into the slope

Why it works

  • Main walkway between classes, with heavy student foot traffic.
  • Right beside the directory, where visitors already stop to look.
  • The lawn and Building 1 make a clean backdrop for photos.
Marked in red · sign is 3 ft × 4 ft
Option 4

Building 4 Wall at the Drop-Off

MountingBolted flat to the wall

Why it works

  • Every car in the drop-off line sees it up close.
  • A wall mount is the simplest install, with no digging.
  • Protected from carts and foot traffic.
Marked in red · sign is 3 ft × 4 ft
Option 5

Track and Field Fence

MountingAttached to the chain-link fence

Why it works

  • Seen by community members who use the track on evenings and weekends.
  • Easy and cheap to attach to the fence.
  • Faces the path along the field.

All five options

Ranked by how many people will see the sign and how easy it is to install. Happy to go with whichever spot you prefer.
